page.layout: One printed page of text (page 51) with a running head at the top; a marginal note at the right beside the lines "que. Psyllorum gens"; a catchword "flu-" at the foot right; a signature "C 2" at the foot. Left edge shows fragments of a neighbouring page's margin, which are not transcribed.

main_text.p: latur manibus, vacillat pedi- ous, totus in gestum abivit Genius: Videtur aliquid vel- le innuere: Quidlibet; Modo ne nobis imponat vastas illas oceani genas, alapis, quas ei Xerxes incussit, livorem suum debere. Sed leve sit sin- gulos aliquos homines dece- pisse; quod subjiciam, populi delirium est, & ejusdem il- lius Genii impostturis ac in- stinctui ascribendum est uti- que. Psyllorum gens, quæ Psyllos in Austrum venusum. propter majores Africæ Syr- tes, sedem habuit, crebris ab Austro vento, damnis & cla- dibus accepti: nunc obtriti domorum arborumque stra- ge, nunc arenarum, velut in flu-
main_text.notes: Left margin shows cropped fragments of another page's text, not transcribed. Words such as "vastas", "imponat" and "impostturis" are printed as they appear; "impostturis" is a probable misprint for "impostura". Marginal note reads "Psyllos in Austrum venusum." as shown.

page.notes: Doubtful: "impostturis" [?]; the note's last word may be "ventum" [?].
